scope: Five selected papers, not exhaustive literature search; identity and published claims verified, underlying market results not independently replicated

papers.title: Investor Sentiment in the Stock Market

locations.construction: PDF pages 11–12 (printed 139–140), levels and changes PCA
locations.results: PDF pages 18–21, especially page 20 (printed 148) aggregate prediction caveat

papers.supports: Levels and changes need separate construction; speculative stocks are more sentiment sensitive; aggregate crash timing remains difficult.
papers.version_note: AEA page range says 129–152, PDF/Crossref says 129–151. Page range omitted from final citation; identity unaffected.

papers.title: Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
papers.version: University-hosted journal PDF; author institutional identity verified

locations.results: PDF pages 11–13 and 21; trading and cost caveat pages 25–26

papers.supports: Media pessimism predicts short-run price pressure and subsequent reversal; gross hypothetical trading results require a separate cost assessment.

numeric_scope.sample: 1984–1999, PDF page 2 and Table II PDF page 11

papers.version_note: Publication year verified against author institutional page and Crossref; no profitability number reproduced.

papers.title: News vs. Sentiment: Predicting Stock Returns from News Stories
papers.version: FULL BODY READ: FEDS 2016-048 dated 2016-06-06, DOI 10.17016/FEDS.2016.048. Journal 2017 identity and abstract checked; final body not claimed identical.

locations.results: PDF pages 12–18, Table 4; earnings and conclusion pages 19–21

papers.supports: Aggregation frequency changes return horizon; positive, negative and no-news effects need separation.

numeric_scope.daily_horizon: 1–2 days; PDF page 2 and Table 3 page 28
numeric_scope.weekly_horizon: Up to 13 weeks, Table 4 and PDF pages 12–14

papers.version_note: 2017 journal metadata verified; 2018 online entry in registry is not substituted for print year. Authors' post-news out-of-sample wording is not reclassified as a fully unseen modern forecasting holdout.

papers.title: The Sum of All FEARS Investor Sentiment and Asset Prices
papers.version: Author-hosted 2014 Advance Access PDF of work in 2015 print issue

locations.results: PDF page 13 Table 2 discussion; timing footnote 14; robustness page 20; conclusion page 29

papers.supports: Search-based fear coincides with falling equity markets and predicts a short-lived reversal; search and return clocks need alignment.
papers.version_note: 2014 advance date and 2015 journal year kept separate; first-day time overlap and robustness acknowledged, not erased.

papers.title: News-based investor disagreement and stock returns
papers.type: Firm-level news-response disagreement and cross-sectional returns
papers.supports: Higher volume-volatility elasticity means lower inferred disagreement; return relation is state dependent and estimation is coverage limited.

numeric_scope.estimation: Trailing 12 months with at least 10 news observations; section 3.2.2

papers.version_note: Section 4.3 includes mixed quintile/decile wording; no silent grouping choice or portfolio replication performed.
